title: Answer to Question: The International Reality with Regard to Ukraine
text:
Answer to Question: The International Reality with Regard to Ukraine

Question:

It is known that Yanukovych is Russia's man in Ukraine, and he is now the president of Ukraine, and the normal thing is that his orientation would be towards Russia. However, it is noticed that his positions are soft towards Europe and America. Does this mean that he has begun to turn towards the West, away from Russia, or is it by agreement with Russia in order to preserve his rule in the face of the interventions and pressures to which Yanukovych is subjected?

Answer:

For the answer to be grasped, it is necessary to know the international reality with regard to Ukraine... Ukraine is the centre of an old struggle between Russia and Europe; then America entered the arena of struggle in the modern era. This conflict, especially between Russia and Europe, has left a deep impact on the people of Ukraine and on their view of the West and Russia. The people who live in the east of the country are loyal to Russia, whereas the people residing in the west of the country are influenced by Europe and America, and consequently the country is actually divided into two parts. Moreover, the political elite in Ukraine has worked over the years on balancing relations between the European powers and Russia, or on siding with the dominant power, whether it is Europe or Russia.

Thus Ukraine is important to these states:

1- As for Russia, Ukraine is one of the most important countries to it, for if it loses it, the West becomes directly on its borders. It is like a protective shield for it from the side of Europe, apart from its economic importance, as the Russian gas pipelines pass through it to the West. It should be known that Russia insists on restoring its hegemony in the region of the Soviet Union, of which Ukraine was a part. But when the so-called Orange Revolution broke out and Yushchenko succeeded in reaching power in the 2005 elections, Russia's influence in Ukraine weakened, for Yushchenko is an American agent, and America exploited the period of his rule to accelerate integration between Ukraine and the West. Throughout the period he spent in office, Yushchenko was threatening to expel the Russian Black Sea Fleet from Sevastopol upon the end of the Russian military lease there in 2017 CE. Yushchenko did not hide his desire to integrate Ukraine fully into Western institutions such as the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation. Kiev entered negotiations on the association agreement with the European Union, and requested a membership action plan for NATO... Thus Russia's influence was in a predicament, but in February 2010 CE it was able to return its man in Ukraine, Viktor Yanukovych, to power. He is the fourth president of the country and a strong supporter of Russia, and from then American influence began to recede, and Ukraine turned towards normalising relations with Russia.

President Yanukovych met the Russian president Medvedev in Kharkov less than two months after assuming his office, on 21/4/2010, and agreed in the meeting to extend the lease of the Black Sea Fleet for 25 additional years, so that it ends in 2042 CE. In return, the Russian company Gazprom agreed to reduce the price of natural gas to 100 dollars per 1,000 m3 for the remaining period of the gas contract that had been signed in 2009 CE. The former Ukrainian prime minister Yulia Tymoshenko objected to the agreements and said that they contradict the constitution, and because of her strong opposition she was put in prison.

Although Ukraine in the era of Yanukovych showed its desire to maintain cooperative relations with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, Yanukovych's government did not request NATO membership or an action plan for reaching membership. With these policies, the bilateral agenda between Kiev and Moscow became in Russia's favour.

On the internal front, Yanukovych's policies have become increasingly authoritarian. On 30 September 2010 CE, the Constitutional Court in Ukraine annulled the amendments that had been introduced to the constitution approved by the Ukrainian parliament in December 2004 CE. This happened after judges who opposed the decision were dismissed and four new judges supporting it were appointed in their place. This allows Yanukovych to return once again to the days before the Orange Revolution, giving this president the power of influence and weakening the authority of parliament.

2- As for Europe, it realises that Russia exploits the gas card and its supply of the West by way of Ukraine; it exploits it for pressure and enticement so that Ukraine remains under Russian influence, or at least does not side with the West at its expense. Therefore Europe tries to entice Ukraine with money and with alternative solutions to its complete dependence on Russian gas. The European Union offered Ukraine money to upgrade the gas infrastructure and technology, and participation in exploiting shale gas, and there came to be talk of making gas the axis of energy. On this background, Ukraine and the European Union signed the protocol of accession to the energy treaties in September 2010 CE, which came into force in February 2011 CE. Earlier this year, Ukraine also signed a 10 billion dollar contract with the Shell company to exploit the shale gas reserve in Ukraine, to be among the largest partnerships in Europe. It is believed that it will be among the largest contracts for extracting underground natural gas from oil shale for the next fifty years in Europe.

Ukraine is currently negotiating with the European Union concerning integration with it, but the Party of Regions (Yanukovych's party) is obstructing these efforts. The head of the European Union delegation to Ukraine (Jan Tombiński) urged the members of the Party of Regions to stop obstructing the work of the parliamentary committee for European integration. Such developments annoy Russia, and to counter the economic incentives of the European Union as part of the integration talks, Russia offered Ukraine to become a member of the customs union. As a result of the Russian pressures and Yanukovych's loyalty to Russia, the Ukrainian parliament ratified on 30-7-2012 the (Russian) free trade area agreement, and Ukraine became the third state, after Russia and Belarus, among the states ratifying this agreement, which had been established on 18/10/2011 and was initially signed by eight states of the Commonwealth of Independent States headed by Russia, and with it Belarus, Ukraine, Armenia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova and Tajikistan. Russia and Belarus ratified it, then Ukraine, and the ratification of the other states follows in succession.

Nevertheless, just as Yanukovych is subjected to Russian pressure, he is likewise subjected to pressures from the European Union, which rejects that Ukraine join the customs union with Russia and further integration with Russia. Therefore the European Union informed Ukraine at the summit that recently brought them together on 25-3-2013 in Brussels that it is not possible to combine membership of the European Union and the customs union. The European Union had facilitated Ukraine's accession to the World Trade Organisation, and Peter Mandelson, the trade commissioner of the European Union, said on 14/1/2013: "The European Union is a strong supporter of Ukraine's membership in the World Trade Organisation, and this is the first step towards greater integration of Ukraine with the global and European economy."

Thus it appears clear that Yanukovych, at the same time as he is loyal to Russia, is also trying to draw closer to the European Union; that is, he is playing on the string of balance between Russian and European interests in Ukraine.

3- As for America, the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 CE created a new opportunity for the old European powers, and likewise for America as a superpower in the world, to exercise greater influence on the political scene in Ukraine. Because of Europe's preoccupation with the reunification of Germany and the unification of the currency in Europe, and its preoccupation with the disputes between the European states, the opportunity was made available to America to exploit the situation to the fullest. Russia was not able in any way to stop America, for it had completely collapsed with the collapse of the Soviet Union and the transformation to capitalism. So America exploited Russia's weakness, and the former president George H. W. Bush signed on 24 October 1992 the Freedom for Russia and Emerging Eurasian Democracies and Open Markets Support Act, which is also known as the Freedom Support Act (FSA), in order to enable the pursuit of a unified American approach in providing aid to the Eurasian countries in the wake of the collapse of the Soviet Union. It entrusted to the Office of the Coordinator of U.S. Assistance to Europe and Eurasia in the State Department (EUR/ACE) the task of coordinating and managing the foreign aid programmes authorised by the Freedom Support Act.

Within the framework of the Freedom Support Act, successive American governments sought to increase their influence in Ukraine. For example, after Ukraine's independence from the Soviet Union in 1991 CE, America was able to use the first president of Ukraine (Leonid Kravchuk) in establishing the trilateral process in 1994 CE to eliminate nuclear weapons on Ukrainian territory. America was also able to establish a strategic partnership with Ukraine through the second president (Leonid Kuchma) in 1994 CE. Kuchma also concluded a partnership and cooperation agreement with the European Union, and agreed to a distinctive partnership with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation. America was even able to influence the bilateral treaty between Russia and Ukraine in May 1997 CE on the question of the rights of the Russian Black Sea Fleet in the Crimean peninsula. America succeeded to a greater extent in Ukraine when President Viktor Yushchenko managed to reach power in the 2005 CE elections in the wake of the Orange Revolution. Yushchenko was an American agent, so America exploited the period of his rule to accelerate integration between Ukraine and the West. Throughout the period he spent in office, Yushchenko was threatening to expel the Russian Black Sea Fleet from Sevastopol after the end of the Russian military lease there in 2017 CE. Yushchenko did not hide his desire to integrate Ukraine fully into institutions such as the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation. Kiev entered negotiations on the association agreement with the European Union, and requested a membership action plan for NATO, but these efforts failed when Russia's man Yanukovych reached power.

Nevertheless, America has continued to pressure Ukraine not to join the Russian customs union, and urges it to join the European Union, because that brings it into the circle of the West and paves the way in the future for bringing Ukraine into NATO, and consequently paves the way for American hegemony over it and limits Russian influence in it; indeed, it creates a ring around Russia from the side of Eastern Europe.

In winning Ukraine, America concentrates on the military aspect by involving it in military manoeuvres, and its final goal is to bring it into the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO). It conducted NATO manoeuvres in the Black Sea on 14/7/2010, which continued until 26-7-2010, in which it involved Ukraine, and that was a few months after the election of Yanukovych and at the peak of his good relations with Russia. The latter, that is Russia, protested against that through its foreign ministry in a statement it issued, saying: "The character of those manoeuvres and the attempt to present them as being against Russia, and the participation in them of states that are not from the region, raise questions and some concern. Likewise, Ukraine's policy aimed at hastening its accession to the Atlantic alliance does not contribute to strengthening good-neighbourly relations." (Iranian radio website 19-7-2010) Likewise, joint American-Ukrainian naval manoeuvres took place on 13-6-2011 for the Ukrainian naval forces in the Black Sea, and likewise "Russia expressed its displeasure in a statement issued by the Russian foreign ministry and considered this step a direct threat to its national security." (Al Arabiya 12-6-2011).

4- We understand from all this that Yanukovych has not cut his connection with Russia and his loyalty to it, but he is not able to fulfil all its demands for it because of the internal and external pressures and because of his keenness to succeed in the 2015 elections. Russia realises that, and it is better for it that Yanukovych remains than that those loyal to the West come, who would work to move away from Russia towards the West, which would expose Russian interests to danger. But Yanukovych will not go far in his relations with the West such that he ends his loyalty to Russia, especially as Yanukovych's popular base is made up of supporters of the orientation towards Russia, so he cannot neglect that. But he will keep working to please the West, to open up to it and to achieve his interests with it. Russia understands that, so it does not tighten its grip too much on Yanukovych, nor does it slacken the rope for him to the extent that he slips out of their hands.
